content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"no","applies_why":"The judge text weighs the challenger's covenant-origin analogy against Matthew 1:20's own statement about the source, rather than using a single verse's silence or treating a two-sense verse as open.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.","room":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. — I weighed whether the judge treats Matthew 1:20 as a two-sense verse that should stand, or instead weighs the challenger's analogy against the verse's contrary statement, which K-S2 does not forbid.","why":"The judge's UNDERDETERMINED rests on a footed challenger analogy weighed against Matthew 1:20's own contrary statement, not on the verse's failure to state a link or on treating a two-sense verse as open."}
